requirements.title: The Compass repo has the Compass Framework
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the Compass repo to carry the same Compass Framework it installs into other projects, generated by the portal itself, so that any person or agent changing Compass follows the same process.
ac:
Given the Compass repository
When I open it
Then it has compass/ (spec.json, intent/, design/, plans/, REVIEW.md, guardrails.json and the checking scripts), AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the PR and issue templates and the Claude Code edit hook

Given the framework files in the repo
When they are compared with what the portal generates for this project
Then they were produced by the portal's own frameworkFiles(), not written by hand

requirements.title: Every pull request is checked by CI
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want every pull request to Compass checked automatically, so that a change without approvals, a plan or tests cannot be merged unnoticed.
ac:
Given a pull request to main
When CI runs
Then it runs the spec check, the guardrails check (main's copy, including the plan check), the unit tests and the build

Given a push to main
When the existing deploy workflow runs
Then the website deploy works exactly as before

requirements.title: The checking scripts have unit tests
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the checking scripts that Compass installs into every project to have their own tests, so that a broken check is caught before it reaches other projects.
ac:
Given the scripts in src/framework/
When npm test runs (Node's built-in runner, no new library)
Then it covers the spec check (traceability, intent, design gate), the plan check and the edit hook's decisions

Given a change that breaks one of these checks
When npm test runs
Then at least one test fails

requirements.title: The installed scripts never drift from the portal's copies
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the checking scripts in the repo's compass/ folder to stay identical to the copies the portal installs (src/framework/), so that Compass is checked by exactly the rules it gives other projects.
ac:
Given compass/check-spec.mjs, compass/check-guardrails.mjs, compass/guardrails-lib.mjs and compass/hooks/guard-edit.mjs
When one differs from its copy in src/framework/
Then npm test fails and names the file

requirements.title: Idea: business need revised into a business intent
requirements.story: As a product owner, I want to write a business need and get it revised into a measurable business intent, so that the work starts from an outcome.
ac:
Given a business need on the Idea page
When the Ideation agent runs and I approve its brief
Then the feature has the revised intent, my original need and a brief, and the Requirements agent starts

requirements.title: Requirements: generate and approve
requirements.story: As a business analyst, I want requirements drafted with Given/When/Then criteria, so that I only review and approve them.
ac:
Given an approved intent
When the Requirements agent runs and its proposal is accepted
Then Draft requirements appear; approving the last one starts the Design agent

requirements.title: Design: design tool, screens and approval gate
requirements.story: As a product owner, I want a design traced to the approved requirements and approved before coding, so that code is built to agreed screens.
ac:
Given a feature whose design is not Approved
When I open Build
Then coding is locked; after Approve design it is unlocked

requirements.title: Test cases: one or more per requirement
requirements.story: As QA, I want test cases generated for every uncovered requirement, so that nothing is built untested.
ac:
Given requirements without test cases
When the Test design agent runs and its proposal is accepted
Then each of them has a happy-path and a negative test case

requirements.title: Build: coding agent, plan file and pull request
requirements.story: As a developer, I want the coding agent to propose a change set that passes guardrails and opens a PR with a plan file, so that I only review the diff.
ac:
Given approved requirements and an approved design
When I approve the agent's change set
Then a branch and PR are opened with compass/plans/<REQ-ids>-<name>.md committed first

requirements.title: Release: merge, tag and deploy
requirements.story: As a delivery manager, I want to release several features in one confirmed step, so that releases are consistent.
ac:
Given approved agent PRs with green CI
When I confirm the release
Then they are merged, requirements are marked Done and a vX.Y.Z tag is created

requirements.title: Framework: install into repos without overwriting their own files
requirements.story: As a repo owner, I want Install framework to add only missing files, so that my repo's own scripts and docs are kept.
ac:
Given an existing repo with its own compass/*.mjs
When Install framework runs
Then only missing framework files are added, the generated spec views are refreshed and the repo's own files are listed as kept

requirements.title: The Team floor shows every agent at its desk with its current state
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want one page that shows all seven agents at their desks with their current state, so that I can see at a glance who is working, on which feature, and who waits for me.
ac:
Given a project with agent runs
When I open "Team floor" in the project sidebar
Then I see the seven agents at desks in pipeline order (Ideation, Requirements, Design, Test design, Coding, Review, Release), each with its name, the role it mirrors (Ideation PO, Requirements BA, Design UX, Test design QA, Coding Dev, Review QA, Release DM) and a state badge

Given an agent's latest run
When its status is running, awaiting-approval, approved/done, failed/rejected, or there is no open run
Then its desk shows Working, Waiting for you, Done, Rework or Idle, and the feature it works on

Given the summary above the floor
When runs change state
Then the counts of agents working, runs waiting for approval and features in flight update

Given the feature filter
When I choose one feature
Then only that feature's runs set the desks; desks without a run of that feature show Idle

requirements.title: What each agent is doing appears live in its speech bubble and the activity list
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to see what each working agent is doing right now, so that I can follow the team without opening every run.
ac:
Given an agent with a running run
When a new step is recorded in its trace
Then within 1 second its speech bubble shows that step's title

Given the live activity list
When steps are recorded by any agent
Then the newest step appears at the top with its time, agent and title, and screen readers announce it politely

requirements.title: Handoffs move as cards between desks, and a failed review sends the card back
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to see work moving from one agent to the next, so that I understand the flow and spot rework.
ac:
Given a run whose output passes to the next agent (for example approved requirements start the Design agent)
When the handoff happens
Then a card with the feature or REQ ids moves along the corridor from the first desk to the next one

Given the Review agent fails a change set
When the run goes back to the Coding agent
Then the card moves back along a coral path and the Coding desk shows Rework

requirements.title: Approvals can be given from the Team floor with the same result as from Agent runs
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to approve or reject waiting work straight from the Team floor, so that nothing waits on me longer than needed.
ac:
Given runs awaiting approval
When I look at the Your approval desk
Then it lists the waiting runs (the 3 that have waited longest and "+N more", REQ-061); each item opens its details with "Open run to approve" (REQ-062), and the desk says "Nothing waiting" when there is none

Given a waiting run
When I open it from the Team floor (approval desk or the agent's desk) and approve or reject it
Then the result is exactly the same as approving or rejecting it from Agent runs

requirements.title: The Team floor respects reduced motion, works on a phone and in demo mode, at no extra cost
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the Team floor to be comfortable for everyone and free to run, so that I can use and demo it anywhere.
ac:
Given my device asks for reduced motion, or I press "Pause motion"
When the floor updates
Then nothing moves: desks, bubbles and lists still update and a handoff card simply appears at the next desk

Given a phone-sized screen (below 720 px)
When I open the Team floor
Then an approval banner is on top listing the waiting runs like the desk (REQ-060, REQ-061), the desks are in a 2-column grid in pipeline order and the activity list is collapsed

Given demo mode (no API key)
When agents run
Then the Team floor shows them the same way

Given the Team floor is open
When agents run
Then no extra Claude calls, tokens, network requests or libraries are used: everything comes from the run trace already recorded

requirements.title: Compass colours follow the honey design system in light and dark mode
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want Compass to use the Bee There honey colours, so that both products look like one family.
ac:
Given the design tokens in src/index.css
When I compare them with the Figma page "🎨 Design system" (Honey edition v0.2)
Then the primitive and semantic colours match in light and dark mode, with honey #FFC629 as the brand colour and dark ink text on it

Given any state colour in the portal
When it is shown
Then honey means brand or "your turn", sky means working/info, mint means done/success and coral means rework/error

Given normal text on its background
When contrast is measured in light and dark mode
Then it is at least 4.5:1 (WCAG AA)

requirements.title: Compass type, shapes and logo follow the honey design system
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want Compass to have the same friendly type and shapes as Bee There, so that the brand feels the same, not only the colours.
ac:
Given any heading
When it is shown
Then it uses Lexend SemiBold; body text stays Be Vietnam Pro and ids stay JetBrains Mono

Given buttons, chips, cards and the sidebar
When they are shown
Then buttons and chips are pills, cards use 20–28 px corners and the warm honey-tinted shadow

Given the logo in the sidebar, the mobile top bar and the browser tab
When it is shown
Then it is the honey square with the dark compass needle

requirements.title: No page keeps the old teal theme
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the rebrand to reach every page, so that no screen still looks like the old Compass.
ac:
Given every page of the portal (Projects, Agent architecture, Connections, Feature board, the feature stages, Release, Agent runs, Knowledge)
When I open it in light and dark mode
Then it uses the honey theme

Given the source code in src/
When the unit tests run
Then a test fails if any old teal colour (#EDFAF7, #D2F2EA, #6ECDB9, #38B09A, #0E7666, #0D5E52, #0C3A34) or a hard-coded colour outside the design tokens is found

requirements.title: Draft and Approved labels look different at a glance
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want Draft and Approved labels of requirements and designs in different colours, so that I see at a glance what still needs my approval.
ac:
Given a requirement with status Draft (on the Requirements, Test cases, Feature or Build page) or a feature design with status Draft (Design page)
When its status label is shown
Then it uses the neutral (grey) tone

Given a requirement or a feature design with status Approved, on the same pages
When its status label is shown
Then it uses the success (mint) tone, like Done, in light and dark mode; In build stays info (sky)

Given the status labels (neutral, info and success tones)
When contrast is measured
Then their text keeps at least 4.5:1 on the label background in light and dark mode

requirements.title: The stage strip of a feature reads well on a phone
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the stage strip of a feature to stay readable on my phone, so that I can follow a feature anywhere.
ac:
Given a feature page on a screen narrower than 720 px
When the stage strip (Idea → Release) is shown
Then each stage takes the full width in one list, in stage order, and no word is broken across lines

Given a screen 720 px or wider
When the stage strip is shown
Then it looks as it does today

requirements.title: Delete a feature from its page after typing its id
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to delete a feature from its page, so that a feature added by mistake does not stay on the board for good.
ac:
Given a feature page
When I click "Delete feature" (next to "Archive feature")
Then a dialog lists what will be removed: the feature's requirements, test cases, files (compass/intent, features and design F-xxx.md) and its open GitHub issues

Given the delete dialog
When the text I type is not exactly the feature id (e.g. F-012)
Then the Delete button stays disabled

Given the delete dialog
When I press Esc or Cancel
Then the dialog closes and nothing is changed

Given I typed the feature id
When I click Delete
Then the feature is removed and I am back on the feature board, which no longer shows it

Given the dialog on a phone (390 px) or with the keyboard only
When I use it
Then it fits the screen, focus stays inside the dialog and every button can be reached with Tab

requirements.title: Deleting a feature removes everything that belongs to it
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want everything of a deleted feature removed from the spec and the repo, so that nothing is left behind and the checks stay green.
ac:
Given a feature is deleted
When the spec is updated
Then the feature, its requirements (featureId = the feature), its test cases and its agent runs are removed; a test case that also covers a requirement of another feature is kept without the deleted ids

Given a decision (ADR) references a deleted requirement
When the feature is deleted
Then the decision is kept and only the deleted ids are taken out of its reqIds

Given a project on GitHub
When the feature is deleted
Then one commit updates compass/spec.json and its views and deletes compass/intent, compass/features and compass/design F-xxx.md of that feature (only the ones that exist), and node compass/check-spec.mjs passes on the result

Given a demo project or a project without a repo
When the feature is deleted
Then it is removed locally and nothing is sent to GitHub

requirements.title: The deleted feature's open GitHub issues are closed as not planned
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the GitHub tickets of a deleted feature closed, so that the issue list does not show work that will never happen.
ac:
Given a feature is deleted in a project on GitHub
When its issues are looked up
Then every open issue (not pull request) whose title starts with one of the feature's REQ ids (e.g. "REQ-016: …" or "REQ-016, REQ-017: …") or names the feature id (e.g. "(F-012)") is selected, and no other issue

Given the selected issues
When the feature is deleted
Then each gets a comment that the feature was deleted in Compass on that date, and is closed with the reason "not planned"

Given GitHub refuses to close an issue (for example the token lacks Issues: Read & write)
When the feature is deleted
Then the feature is still deleted and the portal lists the issues that are still open, with links and the reason

Given the Connect page, or the error shown when GitHub refuses for lack of permission
When I read the token help
Then it asks for Issues: Read & write as well

requirements.title: A strong warning before deleting a feature that has code
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want a clear warning when a feature I am deleting is already built, so that I know its code and tests still need a clean-up.
ac:
Given a feature with a requirement In build or Done
When the delete dialog opens
Then a red warning names those requirements and says that code and tests in the repo still reference them and need a separate change

Given a feature with open agent pull requests
When the delete dialog opens
Then the pull requests are listed with links, and deleting the feature does not close or merge them

Given a feature whose requirements are all Draft or Approved and that has no open pull request
When the delete dialog opens
Then no warning is shown

requirements.title: Pages use up to 1600 px on large screens and stay responsive
requirements.design: none: width limit and padding only — every page keeps its approved layout
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want Compass pages to use the width of my large screen, so that wide pages like the Team floor are not squeezed next to an empty band.
ac:
Given a screen 1920 px wide
When I open any portal page
Then the content area is up to 1600 px wide (it was 1240 px)

Given a screen between 900 px and 1600 px wide
When I open any page
Then the content fills the available width, side padding shrinks smoothly, and there is no sideways scrolling

Given a phone or a screen below 900 px
When I open any page
Then the layout is the same as before

Given a form page that sets its own reading width (New project, Connections)
When it is shown on a large screen
Then it keeps that reading width

requirements.title: The Ideation agent writes "Done when" and never invents a baseline or target
requirements.design: none: agent instructions and framework text, no UI
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the Ideation agent to say what will be true when the change is done instead of inventing numbers, so that I can judge and approve a brief without making up a baseline or target.
ac:
Given a business need
When the Ideation agent drafts a brief
Then the intent says who and what changes, "Done when" says what will be true afterwards, and there is no baseline or target unless the need itself gives numbers or names the change a bet

Given no AI key (the offline draft)
When a brief is drafted
Then it has no "[baseline %]", "[target %]" or "baseline → target" placeholders

Given the framework text Compass installs (AGENTS.md and compass/intent/README.md)
When an agent reads it
Then it asks every intent for "## Done when" and a metric with a baseline only for a bet the Product Owner names, the same rule as travel-map REQ-059

requirements.title: The Idea page and briefs say "Done when" instead of "Outcome metric"
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the Idea page and briefs to ask what will be true when it is done, so that the form no longer asks me for a baseline → target.
ac:
Given the Idea page
When I look at the brief fields
Then "Outcome metric (baseline → target)" is called "Done when (and optional signal to watch)" and no label or help text asks for a baseline → target

Given an Ideation agent run brief and the generated compass/features/F-xxx.md and compass/intent/F-xxx.md
When they show the brief
Then the heading reads "Done when" instead of "Outcome metric" or "Success measure"

requirements.title: Figma components on the Components page, one section per feature
requirements.design: none: rule for the Figma file and framework text, no UI
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want every Figma component on the "Components" page and each feature's screens grouped in one Figma section, so that I review a feature at a glance and find reusable pieces in one place.
ac:
Given the project Figma file
When an agent creates or finds a component (component or component set)
Then it lives on the "Components" page, never on a feature, prototype or brand page, and an instance stays where it was shown

Given a new feature with UI
When an agent draws its screens
Then all of them sit inside one Figma section named "<F-xxx / REQ ids> · <topic>", and the design links that section

Given the framework text Compass installs (compass/design/README.md) and AGENTS.md
When an agent reads it
Then it states both rules, the same as travel-map REQ-061

requirements.title: Each waiting item says what it is and how long it has waited
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want each waiting item on the Team floor to say what it is about and how long it has waited, so that I can tell them apart without opening them.
ac:
Given a run waiting for approval
When it is listed on the Your approval desk (or the phone banner)
Then the item shows the agent, the feature, one line of the run's goal (cut with … when longer) and how long it has waited since it started waiting ("now" under a minute, then "6m", "2h", "2d")

Given two waiting runs of the same agent and feature
When they are listed
Then their goals tell them apart

Given a waiting run blocked by a guardrail
When it is listed
Then the item is marked "blocked", and its side panel shows "Open run · blocked" instead of "Open run to approve"

requirements.title: The approval desk stays compact, with a link to all waiting runs
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the approval desk to stay the same size however many runs wait, so that the floor keeps its shape.
ac:
Given more than 3 runs waiting for approval
When the Team floor is shown
Then the desk (and the phone banner) lists the 3 that have waited longest (by the time they started waiting) and a "+N more → Agent runs" link

Given the "+N more" link
When I click it
Then Agent runs opens showing only the runs awaiting approval, with a way to show all runs again

Given 3 or fewer runs waiting
When the desk is shown
Then all of them are listed and there is no "+N more" link

requirements.title: Details of a waiting item open in a side panel
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to read the details of a waiting item without leaving the Team floor, so that I decide quickly what to approve first.
ac:
Given a waiting item on the desk or the phone banner
When I click it
Then a side panel opens (full screen on a phone) with the agent and feature, the waiting time, the full goal, a short summary of the proposal (idea brief, number of requirements, design screens or test cases, or number of changed files, from the run's proposal and change set) and the guardrail and evaluation results

Given the side panel
When I choose "Open run to approve" ("Open run · blocked" for a blocked run, REQ-060)
Then the run page opens, where approving or rejecting works exactly as from Agent runs; the panel itself has no Approve button

Given the side panel is open
When I press Escape, click outside it or choose Close
Then it closes and keyboard focus returns to the item I opened it from

requirements.title: The sidebar is grouped, has icons and shows the open project as a card
requirements.story: As any portal user, I want the sidebar grouped with an icon on every link and the open project shown as a card, so that I find a page and see the project's state at a glance.
ac:
Given any page of the portal on a desktop screen
When I look at the sidebar
Then it shows three groups separated by a line — workspace (Projects, Agent architecture), the open project (only when one is open) and an account footer at the bottom — and every page link starts with an icon

Given a project is open
When I look at the project group
Then a card shows the project's first letter, its name and its state ("Demo project", the GitHub sync state such as "Synced with GitHub" or "Sync failed", or "Local project" when it is not on GitHub), and clicking it opens the project list

Given a project is open
When I look under the project card
Then the links are, in order, Feature board, Team floor, Agent runs, Release and Project settings (REQ-075: no Knowledge link; ADR-015: Project settings last, after the Admin-only Team link once Team access adds it)

Given I use the keyboard
When I press Tab through the sidebar in light or dark mode
Then every link, card and button shows a visible focus ring

requirements.title: The approval count shows once, on Team floor
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want one clear count of the agent runs waiting for my approval, so that the same number shown twice does not look like two different things to do.
ac:
Given N agent runs of the open project wait for approval (N > 0)
When I look at the sidebar
Then only Team floor shows a count pill with N, announced as "N waiting for approval", with a tooltip saying N agent run(s) wait for my approval, and Agent runs shows no count

Given no agent run waits for approval
When I look at the sidebar
Then no count is shown

requirements.title: The feature list is readable
requirements.story: As any portal user, I want to read each feature's name and stage in the sidebar, so that I can open the right feature without guessing from a cut-off name.
ac:
Given a project with features
When I look at the sidebar
Then a "Features" heading shows how many features are listed, and each feature shows a dot in its stage colour, its name on up to two lines and its short id (e.g. F01) on the right

Given I hover a feature
When the tooltip shows
Then it gives the feature id, the full name and the stage

Given a feature is open
When I look under it
Then its five stages (Idea, Requirements, Design, Test cases, Build) are listed indented, each with its step number or ✓ when done

requirements.title: The account footer shows the connection, the role and one theme button
requirements.story: As any portal user, I want my GitHub connection, my role and the theme together at the bottom of the sidebar, so that settings are in one tidy place.
ac:
Given GitHub is connected as @user and sign-in is off
When I look at the bottom of the sidebar
Then an account card shows the initial, "@user" and "GitHub connected"; without a connection it shows "Not connected" and "Demo mode · connect"; clicking the card opens the account menu, whose "Connections" item opens Connections (REQ-110, ADR-019)

Given the footer
When I open the account menu
Then it has one theme control, a "Dark theme" switch titled "Switch to dark theme" (or "Switch to light theme"), and choosing it switches the theme; the role picker sits above the card only with sign-in off or in the demo (REQ-110, ADR-019)

Given a phone (below 900 px)
When I open the Menu
Then the sidebar shows the same groups, card and footer

requirements.title: The portal shows no "AI dev portal" tagline
requirements.story: As the Product Owner, I want the portal to present itself as "Compass" only, so that the "AI dev portal" tagline is not shown anywhere in the product.
ac:
Given any page of the portal
When I look at the sidebar brand
Then it shows the logo and "Compass" with no "AI dev portal" line under it

Given the onboarding page
When I look at the overline above the title
Then it reads "Compass" and no screen of the portal shows the text "AI dev portal"

requirements.title: The sidebar has no Knowledge link for any role
requirements.story: As any portal user, I want the sidebar to show only the pages of the delivery flow, so that the technical Knowledge (RAG) page does not distract me.
ac:
Given a project is open, in any role (PO, BA, DM, UX, Dev, QA, Ops)
When I look under the project card
Then the links are, in order, Feature board, Team floor, Agent runs, Release and Project settings (ADR-015), and there is no Knowledge link

Given the address /p/<project>/knowledge
When I open it directly
Then the Knowledge page still opens, and agent runs keep indexing and searching the repository as before

requirements.title: Quote any part of an agent run
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to quote part of an agent's answer, so that I can point at exactly what I want explained or changed.
ac:
Given an agent run with an answer (idea brief, requirements, design, test cases, summary or a file of the change set)
When I select text inside the answer
Then a "Quote" button appears next to the selection

Given a selection
When I click "Quote"
Then a new reply card opens under the run with the selected text and its source (e.g. "REQ-051 · AC 2", "SCR-2 · states", "src/app.ts"), and its message field gets the focus; each quote gets its own card

Given a requirement, screen, test case or file in the answer
When I click its "Quote" icon
Then a reply card opens with the whole item as its quote, without selecting text

Given several open reply cards
When I click "Cancel" on one card, or press Esc while the focus is in it
Then only that card closes, nothing is sent to the agent, and the other cards stay as they were

Given the trace, text outside the answer, or a run that is still working
When I select text there
Then no "Quote" button appears

Given a phone (390 px) or the keyboard only
When I long-press to select text, or Tab to an item's "Quote" icon and press Enter
Then a reply card opens the same way, in the page under the answer, and scrolls into view

requirements.title: Ask the agent about the quoted text
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to ask the agent for more details about what I quoted, so that I understand its answer before I approve it.
ac:
Given a reply card (its quote and an optional message), or a question typed in the "Ask the agent" box
When I click "Ask" on it
Then my message with its quote appears in the run's conversation, the agent's answer appears under it, and that card closes while other cards stay

Given the agent answered a question
When I look at the proposal
Then it is unchanged and the run keeps its status (e.g. awaiting approval)

Given a live run
When the agent answers
Then the follow-up sends the run's goal, its proposal, the conversation so far, the quotes and my message — not a new repository index — and the answer shows its token count

Given a project in demo mode (no API key)
When I click "Ask"
Then a predictable demo answer that repeats the quoted sources appears

Given an empty "Ask the agent" box (no quote and no message)
When I look at it
Then its "Ask" button is disabled; a reply card can always be sent, because it has a quote

requirements.title: Revise the proposal from the quoted text
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want the agent to revise only what I quoted, so that I keep the good parts of its proposal.
ac:
Given a run awaiting approval and a reply with quotes
When I click "Revise"
Then the agent produces a new version of the proposal that changes the quoted items as the message asks and keeps every other item unchanged

Given a revision of requirements, test cases or design screens
When it is saved
Then existing ids are kept (REQ-xxx, TC-xxx, SCR-x) and only new items get new ids

Given a coding agent run
When I revise with a quote from one file
Then only the quoted files are proposed again and the other files of the change set stay as they were

Given a revision
When it is saved
Then the guardrails and evaluations run again on the new version and the run is awaiting approval

Given a rejected run
When I revise it
Then the run is awaiting approval again with the new version

Given an approved run
When I look at the reply box
Then "Revise" is disabled with the hint "Already applied — start a new run" and "Ask" still works

requirements.title: Proposal versions and compare
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to see what changed between proposal versions, so that I can check a revision quickly.
ac:
Given a revision
When it is saved
Then the conversation shows a marker "Proposal v2 — changed: …" naming the changed items (e.g. "REQ-051 · AC 2", "src/app.ts")

Given a run with two or more versions
When I click "Compare with v1"
Then the changed items are shown as a diff with the previous version (removed lines red, added lines mint), and unchanged items are folded

Given a run with several versions
When I pick an earlier version
Then I can read it, and the run marks which version is the latest

Given a run with several versions
When I click Approve
Then the latest version is applied (spec merge or pull request), never an earlier one

requirements.title: The conversation is kept with the run, safely
requirements.story: As a team member, I want the conversation with an agent to stay with its run, so that anyone can see why the proposal changed.
ac:
Given a run with a conversation
When I reload the portal or open the run from the Runs page or the Team floor
Then the conversation, its quotes and all proposal versions are still there

Given quoted text or a message that contains instructions (e.g. "ignore previous instructions")
When it is sent to the agent
Then it is wrapped as data, the prompt-injection guardrail runs on it and a warning is shown in the trace

Given a run is deleted
When it is removed
Then its conversation and versions are removed with it

requirements.title: Handoffs are shown on phones too
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to see work move between agents on my phone, so that I can follow the team away from my desk.
ac:
Given a screen narrower than 720 px
When a run is handed to the next agent within the last 4 seconds
Then a strip inside the floor, above the desks, shows "<from agent> [card with the feature or REQ ids] → <to agent>" and the sentence "Handed to the <to agent name> — it starts now" (for example "Handed to the Requirements agent — it starts now"), in honey, and the receiving desk is marked with a honey ring

Given a screen narrower than 720 px
When a review sends a change set back within the last 4 seconds
Then the strip shows "Coding ← [↩ <findings>] Review" and "The review sent the work back to the Coding agent", in coral, and the Coding desk is marked with a coral ring

Given reduced motion or Pause motion
When a handoff is shown on a phone
Then nothing slides: the strip simply appears and disappears after 4 seconds

Given several handoffs within the same 4 seconds
When the strip is shown on a phone
Then it lists each of them, newest first, one line per handoff (at most 3)

Given no handoff in the last 4 seconds, or a screen 720 px or wider
When the Team floor is shown
Then there is no strip (desktop keeps the corridor as today)

requirements.title: The agent trace can be folded and unfolded
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want to fold the step-by-step trace of an agent run, so that I reach the proposal and the approval buttons without scrolling past every tool call.
ac:
Given an agent run that is awaiting approval, approved, rejected, failed or done
When its run view opens
Then the trace is folded to its header, which shows the number of steps (and how many failed, if any) and a "Show steps" toggle

Given an agent run that is still running
When its run view opens
Then the trace is open, as today

Given a run view
When the Product Owner clicks the trace toggle (or presses Enter/Space on it)
Then the trace opens or folds, the toggle reads "Show steps" or "Hide steps" and reports aria-expanded, and each step's own details still expand as before

Given a run that moves from running to awaiting approval while it is shown
When the status changes and the Product Owner has not used the toggle
Then the trace folds; once the toggle was used, her choice is kept

requirements.title: An admin adds a person to a project by email with one or more roles
requirements.story: As a project admin, I want to add a person to my project by email and give them one or more roles, so that they can work on the project in the roles they have.
ac:
Given I am an Admin of the project or the super admin
When I open the project's Team page
Then I see the team list (email, roles) and an "Add person" form with an email field and role checkboxes PO, BA, UX, QA, Dev, DM, Ops and Admin

Given the Add person form
When I enter "Ba@Example.com " and tick BA and QA and click Add
Then ba@example.com appears in the list with the roles BA and QA (email stored trimmed and in lower case)

Given the Add person form
When the email is not a valid address, no role is ticked, or the email is already on the team
Then Add is refused with a message saying why and the list is unchanged

Given I am signed in without the Admin role on this project and I am not the super admin
When I open the project
Then I do not see the Team page in the menu and Firestore refuses any change to its team

Given a project that has no team yet
When anyone other than the super admin tries to create its team
Then Firestore refuses it; only the super admin creates a project's first team and names at least one Admin in it

requirements.title: An admin changes a person's roles or removes them from the project
requirements.story: As a project admin, I want to change someone's roles or remove them, so that access follows the person's current job.
ac:
Given a person on the team
When I change their role checkboxes and save
Then the list shows the new roles and their next action in the portal uses them

Given a person on the team
When I click Remove and confirm
Then they are gone from the list and, at their next page load, no longer see the project

Given the project has only one Admin
When anyone tries to remove that person or untick their Admin role
Then it is refused with "A project needs at least one Admin"

Given I remove a person
When the removal is saved
Then the page reminds me to replace the project's GitHub token, because they may have copied it

requirements.title: People sign in with Google and see only the projects whose team lists their email
requirements.story: As a team member, I want to sign in with my Google account, so that Compass knows which projects and roles are mine.
ac:
Given Firebase is configured and I am not signed in
When I open the portal
Then I see a "Sign in with Google" screen and no project data

Given I sign in with a Google account whose verified email matches a team entry (case-insensitive)
When sign-in completes
Then the Projects page shows only the projects whose team lists my email, and the sidebar account card shows my email; its menu has Sign out

Given I sign in with a Google account that is on no team and is not the super admin
When sign-in completes
Then I see "You have no access yet — ask your admin" with my email and Sign out, and no project data

Given a Google account whose email is not verified
When it signs in
Then it is treated as having no access

Given Firebase is not configured (demo mode)
When I open the portal
Then it works as today without sign-in

requirements.title: Each approval gate can be passed only by a person with the role that owns it
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want each gate tied to its role, so that only the right person can approve each stage.
ac:
Given the gate rules: intent and requirements → PO (BA may also approve requirements); design → UX or PO; test cases → QA; start a build → Dev; merge and release → DM or PO; team and token → Admin
When a signed-in person opens a gate whose role they do not have
Then its button is disabled with the hint "Needs the <role> role"

Given a person with several roles (e.g. BA and QA)
When they open the requirements and test-case gates
Then both are enabled, and the design and release gates are disabled

Given a person changes the page in the browser to enable a disabled gate
When the approval is saved
Then the Firestore rules refuse its approval record (REQ-037), the portal shows "Not allowed for your roles" and nothing is committed to GitHub (an approval committed outside the portal without a record is flagged, REQ-038)

Given the super admin
When they open any gate
Then it is enabled

requirements.title: A project Admin stores one GitHub token that the project's members use
requirements.story: As a project admin, I want to save one GitHub token for the project, so that members without their own GitHub account can save their work to the repo.
ac:
Given I am an Admin of the project
When I open Team → GitHub token
Then I can paste a token, test it and save it; the help asks for a fine-grained token for this repo only, with Contents, Pull requests and Issues: Read & write and an expiry date

Given a saved project token and a signed-in member without their own token
When they approve requirements and the portal commits
Then the commit is made with the project token and approvedBy names the member

Given a member who is not an Admin
When they open the Team page
Then the page shows no token value and no Test or Replace button (their browser can still read the token to make GitHub writes — ADR-011)

Given the token is missing, expired or refused by GitHub
When a member tries a GitHub action
Then the portal says "The project's GitHub token is missing or expired — ask an Admin" and nothing is half-written

requirements.title: The super admin sees every project and can make someone a project Admin
requirements.story: As the super admin, I want to see every project and name its Admins, so that each project can manage its own team.
ac:
Given the super admin's Google email is fixed in the Firestore rules as a one-way hash (the plain email is never in the repo)
When that account, with a verified email, signs in to Compass for the first time
Then the portal records it in the Firestore document config/access, and it sees every project and can open every Team page

Given I am the super admin on a project's Team page
When I tick Admin for a person
Then that person can manage this project's team and token, and no other project's

Given a signed-in person whose email does not match the super admin hash, or is not verified
When the portal tries to create or change config/access
Then Firestore refuses it; once config/access exists, no browser can change it

requirements.title: Every approval records the email and role of the person who gave it
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want every approval to name the person and role, so that the audit trail shows who approved what.
ac:
Given a signed-in person approves an intent, requirement, design, test case or release
When the approval is saved to spec.json
Then approvedBy is "<email> (<role>)", e.g. "ba@example.com (BA)", and approvedAt is the time

Given a person with the Dev role (or the super admin) starts a build
When the build starts
Then its approval record names them (REQ-037) and the agent run shows "Started by <email> (<role>)"; nothing is written to spec.json for a build

Given demo mode without sign-in
When something is approved
Then approvedBy keeps today's value

requirements.title: Each approval is recorded in Firebase, whose rules accept it only from the owning role
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want every approval checked by Firebase before it is saved, so that a role check cannot be skipped by changing the page.
ac:
Given a signed-in person passes a gate (intent, requirements, design, test cases, build or release)
When the portal saves the approval
Then it first writes an approval record to Firestore (project, item ids, gate, email, role, time) and commits to GitHub, or starts the build, only after Firestore accepts it

Given a person without a role that owns the gate, who is not the super admin
When an approval record is written for that gate
Then the Firestore rules refuse it, the portal shows "Not allowed for your roles" and nothing is committed

Given a signed-in person writes an approval record
When the record's email is not their own verified sign-in email, or its role is neither one of their roles on that project that owns the gate nor "super admin" written by the account listed in config/access
Then the Firestore rules refuse it (a BA cannot record "po@example.com (PO)" or "ba@example.com (super admin)"; the super admin can record "<email> (super admin)" for any gate)

Given an approval record exists
When anyone tries to change or delete it
Then the Firestore rules refuse it

Given Firestore accepted the record but the GitHub commit fails
When the portal reports the error
Then the approval is shown as not saved and retrying reuses the same record

requirements.title: Approvals in the repo that Firebase does not confirm are flagged
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want approvals made outside the portal to stand out, so that a forged approvedBy is noticed.
ac:
Given the super admin saves a project's first team
When the team is created
Then the portal stores in Firebase, in the same write as the first team, a baseline of the approvals already in spec.json (item, gate, approvedBy); the Firestore rules accept the baseline only from the super admin, only together with the first team, and refuse any later change or delete

Given the project has a team
When the portal loads the project
Then every approval in spec.json that is neither in the baseline nor matched by an approval record (same item, gate, email and role) shows a red "Unconfirmed" badge naming who it claims, whatever date it claims; if the project has a team but no baseline, every approval without a matching record is flagged

Given unconfirmed approvals exist
When a person opens the project's Feature board
Then a notice lists them with links, so a person with the owning role can approve again

Given demo mode, or approvals listed in the baseline
When the project loads
Then they are not flagged

requirements.title: With sign-in on, roles come from the team instead of the role picker
requirements.story: As the product owner, I want people's roles to come only from the team list, so that nobody can give themselves a role by picking it.
ac:
Given Firebase is configured and a person signs in
When the portal opens
Then the "What's your role?" screen is not shown and their roles on each project come from that project's team

Given a signed-in person on a real project
When they look at the sidebar
Then the account card shows their roles on that project read-only, as chips (ADR-019), and nothing in the portal lets them change their own roles

Given Firebase is not configured
When the portal opens
Then the "What's your role?" screen and the sidebar role picker work as today

requirements.title: A signed-in person can try the demo with a role of their choice
requirements.story: As someone who has signed in but is not on a team yet, I want to try Compass in a role of my choice, so that I can see how it works before my admin adds me.
ac:
Given a signed-in person who is on no team
When they see "You have no access yet"
Then the screen also offers "Try the demo"

Given a signed-in person clicks "Try the demo" on the no-access screen (the sidebar has no "Try the demo", ADR-019)
When the demo opens
Then they pick a role on the "What's your role?" screen and see only the sample demo projects, with a banner "Demo — sample data, kept in this browser only" and "Leave demo"

Given the demo is open
When the person changes their demo role in the sidebar, approves gates or edits the sample project
Then it works like demo mode today: nothing is read from or written to Firebase or GitHub, and no real project, team or token is shown

Given the demo is open
When the person clicks "Leave demo"
Then they return to their projects, or to "You have no access yet" if they are on no team

requirements.title: The admin links the project's Figma file and Miro board on a Project settings page
requirements.story: As the project admin, I want to set the project's Figma file and Miro board once on the project's settings page, so that everyone on the project works from the right design files.
ac:
Given a project is open
When I look at the sidebar
Then the project group ends with a "Project settings" link with a gear icon, for every role: after Release, and after the Admin-only Team link once Team access adds it (ADR-015); it opens the Project settings page

Given I am the project admin: with sign-in on, the project's Admin or the super admin; with sign-in off (demo or local use), the PO role picked in the sidebar
When I open Project settings
Then a "Design files" card shows a Figma file field and a Miro board field, both optional, and I can save, change or clear each one; the saved links are written to compass/spec.json → designTool

Given I enter a Figma link that is not an https link on figma.com or www.figma.com to a design, file, proto or board, or a Miro link that is not an https://miro.com/app/board/ link
When I save
Then the field shows an error naming the link expected and nothing is saved

Given I am not the project admin (with sign-in on: not the project's Admin nor the super admin; with sign-in off: a role other than PO)
When I open Project settings
Then the "Design files" card shows the linked files with an "Open ↗" button each, no edit fields, and the hint "Only the project admin can change the design files"

requirements.title: Every Design page keeps the preview in focus and shows the design files behind a button
requirements.story: As anyone working on a feature's design, I want the Design page to focus on the preview and keep the project's Figma and Miro links one click away, so that I can open the right file without clutter.
ac:
Given a project with a Figma link, a Miro link or both
When I open any feature's Design page
Then there is no design-files card on the page: a "Design files" button with the number of linked files sits at the top right, next to the page title, and the preview takes the full width of the page

Given I am on the Design page
When I press "Design files" (labelled "Files" on a phone)
Then a side panel (a bottom sheet on a phone) lists each linked tool with an "Open ↗" button and no edit fields, plus "Change in Project settings →" for the admin only; Esc, ✕ or a click outside closes it and focus returns to the button

Given a Miro board is linked
When I open the Design page
Then the board is previewed with Miro's live embed; a Figma file or the feature's Figma frame link is previewed with the Figma embed as today; the switch shows only when both are linked; on a phone the preview fits the screen width

Given no design file is linked
When I open the Design page
Then the button reads "Design files · none", the preview area says "No design files linked yet", and the admin also sees a link to Project settings

requirements.title: Projects with the old single design link keep working, and agents name both files
requirements.story: As a team with an existing project, I want my current design link to keep working and the agents to know both design files, so that nothing has to be fixed by hand.
ac:
Given a compass/spec.json whose designTool has only kind and url (Figma, Penpot, Sketch or Other)
When the portal opens the project
Then that link is shown under its tool on Project settings and the Design page, and saving the Miro link keeps designTool.kind and designTool.url unchanged

Given a project with a Figma file and a Miro board linked
When the design agent runs or the portal generates AGENTS.md
Then both tools and their links are named in the agent's prompt and in AGENTS.md

requirements.title: Acceptance criteria and test steps are readable on the agent run page
requirements.design: none: text size only — the run page keeps its approved layout
requirements.story: As the Product Owner, I want the acceptance criteria and test steps an agent proposes to be easy to read, so that I can check them before I approve without zooming in.
ac:
Given an agent run that proposes requirements
When its acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then lines) are shown on the run page
Then they are 13 px with 20 px line height, the same size as the story text above them, and keep their line breaks

Given an agent run that proposes test cases
When their steps are shown on the run page
Then they use the same 13 px size and keep their line breaks

Given any other small monospace text in the portal (ids, file paths, times, design elements)
When it is shown
Then its size is unchanged (11 px)

requirements.title: The project list keeps only one demo project
requirements.design: none: no new screen — the Projects page keeps its approved layout
requirements.story: As the Product Owner, I want only one demo project in my project list, so that the list stays tidy however often I open the demo.
ac:
Given the project list already has the demo project
When I click "Open demo project" or "Explore the demo"
Then that demo project opens and no second copy is added

Given the project list has no demo project
When I click "Open demo project"
Then one demo project is added and opened

Given this browser saved several demo projects before this change
When Compass loads
Then only the most recently added demo project is kept, and every real project stays

requirements.title: The sidebar footer is one account card that opens an account menu
requirements.story: As any portal user, I want one tidy account card at the bottom of the sidebar with my account actions behind it, so that I see who I am and my roles at a glance without a crowded footer.
ac:
Given I am signed in with Google
When I look at the bottom of the sidebar
Then I see one account card with my initial, my name (the part of my email before "@") and my roles on the open project as chips ("Super admin" for the super admin), and no "Try the demo", "Sign out", "My roles" line or separate theme button

Given the account card
When I click it (or press Enter or Space on it)
Then a menu opens with my full email, "Connections" with the GitHub state, a "Dark theme" switch and "Sign out"; in the demo it also has "Leave demo"; it never has "Try the demo"

Given the account menu is open
When I choose an item, press Escape or click outside it
Then the menu closes; "Dark theme" switches the theme, "Connections" opens Connections and "Sign out" signs me out

Given the account menu is open and focus is in it
When I press ArrowDown or ArrowUp
Then focus moves to the next or previous item and wraps around at the ends; from the header at the top of the menu (my name and email, or the account state with sign-in off), ArrowDown goes to the first item and ArrowUp to the last

Given sign-in is off, or I am in the demo
When I look at the footer
Then the role picker is shown above the account card, and the menu has no "Sign out" when sign-in is off

Given a phone (below 900 px)
When I open the Menu
Then the footer and its account menu work the same, within the menu width

tests.title: Framework files present and generated by frameworkFiles()
tests.gherkin:
Given the setup PR
When I list its files
Then compass/, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the templates and .claude/settings.json are present
And the PR describes the generator run that produced them

tests.title: CI runs the spec check, guardrails, tests and build on a PR
tests.gherkin:
Given a pull request to main
When Compass CI runs
Then the steps Spec traceability check, Guardrails check, Test and Build appear in the run

tests.title: Unit tests for check-spec, the plan check and the edit hook
tests.gherkin:
Given the scripts in src/framework/
When npm test runs
Then tests for check-spec (traceability, intent, design gate), planProblems and decideEdit pass
And breaking any of these checks makes a test fail

tests.title: compass/*.mjs identical to src/framework/
tests.gherkin:
Given the checking scripts in compass/ and src/framework/
When npm test runs
Then each pair is byte-identical, and a difference fails the test naming the file

tests.title: Need → intent in the demo
tests.gherkin:
Given the demo project, feature F-003
When I enter a business need and approve the Ideation agent's brief
Then the intent is revised into a measurable outcome and the Requirements agent starts

tests.title: Approve all requirements starts the Design agent
tests.gherkin:
Given Draft requirements
When I click Approve all drafts
Then the Design agent starts

tests.title: Build locked until the design is approved
tests.gherkin:
Given a feature with a Draft design
When I open Build
Then 'Coding is locked' is shown; after Approve design it is gone

tests.title: Test cases generated for uncovered requirements
tests.gherkin:
Given requirements without tests
When the Test design agent runs in demo mode
Then each gets a happy-path and an invalid-input test case

tests.title: Agent PR carries a plan file
tests.gherkin:
Given an approved change set on a connected repo
When the PR is opened
Then compass/plans/<REQ-ids>-<name>.md is in the commit and linked from the PR body

tests.title: Release marks requirements Done and tags
tests.gherkin:
Given approved PRs with green CI
When I release
Then the requirements are Done and a release tag exists

tests.title: Install keeps travel-map's own files
tests.gherkin:
Given travel-map's file list
When the install rule runs
Then 18 of its own files are kept and only the spec views are written

tests.title: Desks show each agent's state from its latest run
tests.gherkin:
Given demo runs in each status (running, awaiting-approval, done, failed) and an agent with no run
When the Team floor state is computed
Then the desks show Working, Waiting for you, Done, Rework and Idle, in pipeline order, each with its name and role (Ideation PO … Release DM) and the feature id
And the summary shows 1 agent working and 1 run waiting for approval
When the running run changes to awaiting-approval
Then the summary shows 0 working and 2 waiting

tests.title: Feature filter limits the desks to one feature
tests.gherkin:
Given runs for F-008 and F-009
When the filter is set to F-009
Then desks with only F-008 runs show Idle and the summary counts only F-009

tests.title: A new step reaches the bubble within 1 second
tests.gherkin:
Given the Team floor open in demo mode
When I start the Coding agent
Then its bubble shows each new step title within 1 second and the activity list adds it at the top
And the activity list is a polite live region (aria-live="polite"), so a screen reader announces each new step without interrupting

tests.title: Handoff and rework cards
tests.gherkin:
Given demo mode
When requirements are approved and later a review fails
Then a card moves Requirements → Design, and later Review → Coding along a coral path with the Coding desk in Rework

tests.title: Approving or rejecting from the floor equals doing it from Agent runs
tests.gherkin:
Given two runs awaiting approval
When I open the first from its approval-desk item (side panel → "Open run to approve") and the second from its agent's desk, and approve the first and reject the second on the run page
Then each run, the spec and the next agent are exactly as when approved or rejected from Agent runs

tests.title: Reduced motion, Pause motion and phone layout
tests.gherkin:
Given prefers-reduced-motion on (and separately Pause motion pressed)
When a handoff happens
Then nothing animates and the card appears at the next desk
And at 390 px wide the banner, 2-column grid and collapsed activity are shown

tests.title: No extra requests from the Team floor
tests.gherkin:
Given a live project (API key set) and the browser network panel
When agents run with the Team floor open, and again with it closed
Then the Claude calls and tokens per run are the same, the Team floor makes no network requests of its own, and package.json gains no new dependency

tests.title: Your approval desk lists waiting runs, or says Nothing waiting
tests.gherkin:
Given two runs awaiting approval (Requirements · F-009, Design · F-008)
When the Team floor state is computed
Then the Your approval desk lists both runs with agent and feature, each opening its details (amended by REQ-061/REQ-062, 2026-11-27)
And when no run awaits approval, the desk says "Nothing waiting"

tests.title: Who is working and what waits for me, at a glance
tests.gherkin:
Given the Team floor in demo mode with one agent working and one run waiting for approval
When the Product Owner looks at it for the first time
Then within 5 seconds she can say which agent is working, on which feature, and what waits for her approval

tests.title: Tokens match the honey design system
tests.gherkin:

decisions.title: Compass follows its own delivery process
decisions.context: Compass enforced the AI-native SDLC in other repos but not on its own code.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner approved the intent: Compass's own repo gets the Compass Framework generated by the portal itself, CI on every pull request, tests for the checking scripts and a no-drift check between compass/ and src/framework/.
decisions.consequences: Every later Compass PR needs an approved intent, approved requirements, a design (or none: <reason>), a plan file and an independent review. The setup PR is larger than 12 files because the check does not exist on main yet.

decisions.title: Light baseline for the existing portal
decisions.context: The portal existed before its repo had a spec.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose a light baseline: one feature per stage (F-001…F-007) with one Done requirement each (REQ-101…107); detailed requirements are written only for new work.
decisions.consequences: Older behaviour is documented at stage level only; new work starts at REQ-001.

decisions.title: Team floor is a live view of the existing run trace
decisions.context: The Product Owner asked for a realtime "creative team" interface like those other AI users built.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner approved the intent for option 1: a Team floor page drawn only from the run trace Compass already records. Agents talking to each other and multi-device viewing are out of scope, each needing its own decision.
decisions.consequences: No change to agents, tools, guardrails or approval gates; no extra Claude cost; live only in the browser tab that runs the agents.

decisions.title: Compass shares the Bee There honey brand on every page
decisions.context: The Team floor design was drawn in a new Figma file; the Product Owner asked for the Bee There look with its signature honey yellow.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose to rebrand all Compass pages (not only the Team floor) to the Honey edition of the design system in the Figma file "Compass — Team floor", which becomes the project design tool. Honey means brand and "your turn"; working moves from amber/teal to sky so the two never look alike.
decisions.consequences: The teal theme is retired; the colour tokens in src/index.css follow the Figma variables; a test keeps old teal out of src/. Where Bee There's text colours fall below WCAG AA 4.5:1 (grey #8A8072, brand text #A87400, and the state texts on pale honey), Compass uses one shade darker; the Product Owner approved this on 2026-11-26.

decisions.title: Intents say "Done when"; a baseline and target only for bets
decisions.context: The Ideation agent asked every business intent for "baseline → target, by when" and invented numbers with no data behind them (e.g. "0% → 20% within 90 days" for a Bee There feature). The Product Owner found them hard to judge.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner decided on 2026-11-27 (same rule as travel-map ADR-021): every intent has a "Done when" in plain words. A small feature may add one optional signal to watch without a target; a process change has "Done when" only; only a change she names a bet gets a metric with its current value, and its target is set after a few weeks of real data. The Ideation agent never invents a baseline or target.
decisions.consequences: The Ideation agent prompt, its offline draft, the installed framework text and the Idea page change; the stored field outcomeMetric keeps its name so existing briefs need no migration. Existing briefs keep their text until the agent is re-run.

decisions.title: Quote and revise: every agent, with versions
decisions.context: F-020 lets the reviewer quote part of an agent answer and Ask or Revise. Two scope questions came up before the requirements were written.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner decided in chat on 2026-11-27: (1) every agent can be quoted and revised, including the coding agent, whose revision re-proposes only the quoted files; (2) a revision creates versions v1, v2… with a compare view, and Approve always applies the latest version. A revision may change only the quoted items; anything else is refused.
decisions.consequences: Runs keep a conversation and their versions. A revised version waits for its guardrails before it can be approved. The Ask and Revise of live runs cost Claude tokens, shown per answer.

decisions.title: Figma file layout: one Components page, one section per feature
decisions.context: Components were spread over the prototype, design-system and feature pages of the "Compass — Team floor" Figma file, and feature screens lay loose on the canvas, which made reviews hard to follow.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner decided in chat on 2026-11-27: every Figma component lives on the "Components" page, and each feature gets one Figma section holding all its screens, for this and every future feature. Same rule as travel-map REQ-061 / ADR-022.
decisions.consequences: Existing components were moved (instances left where they were shown) and existing feature screens grouped; node ids are unchanged, so frame links still work. The design template Compass installs states the rule; CI cannot read Figma, so it is not checked automatically.

decisions.title: Team access uses Firebase on the free Spark plan
decisions.context: Compass is a browser-only app without a server. Team lists and role checks must be shared between people and cannot be trusted if they live only in each browser.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose Firebase Auth (Google sign-in) and Firestore on the free Spark plan, with Firestore security rules as the real gate, over a team.json file in each repo or browser-only storage.
decisions.consequences: New dependency firebase and a firestore rules file (both need the human-approved label); the Product Owner creates the Firebase project and publishes the rules once; ideas, runs and other data stay where they are.

decisions.title: Members use a shared GitHub token per project
decisions.context: GitHub writes need a token. Team members who sign in with Google may have no GitHub account or token.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose one GitHub token per project, stored by its Admins and readable by its members, over each member connecting their own token.
decisions.consequences: Every member's browser can read the token (the Team page only hides it from non-Admins), so a member could copy it and could also commit to the repo without the portal's role checks (see ADR-012); removing them does not revoke that copy. Mitigation: the portal asks for a fine-grained token for that repo only (Contents, Pull requests, Issues) with an expiry date, and reminds Admins to replace it after removing someone.

decisions.title: Approvals are recorded in Firebase and unconfirmed ones are flagged
decisions.context: The independent review of PR #74 found that approvals are commits of spec.json made with the shared project token, so Firestore rules never see them: any member could commit an approval for a gate their role does not own, or forge approvedBy.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose to write every approval to Firestore first (the rules accept it only from the signed-in person's own verified email and a role they hold that owns the gate, or "super admin" for the account in config/access, and records cannot be changed or deleted), commit to GitHub only after that, and flag approvals in spec.json that have neither a matching record nor a place in the baseline stored by the super admin together with the project's first team (only the super admin can create a first team) (dates in the repo are not trusted) — over accepting screen-only checks or going back to personal tokens.
decisions.consequences: Two more requirements (REQ-037, REQ-038). A member with the token can still edit spec.json directly, but such approvals show as Unconfirmed. Known limit: a record names the item and gate, not its content, so editing the text of an already approved item keeps it confirmed; a content fingerprint could be added later. The updated design (Unconfirmed badge) was approved on 2026-11-27. Residual risk: an approval forged into spec.json before the team is first created goes into the baseline and is never flagged.

decisions.title: The super admin is recorded automatically at first sign-in
decisions.context: The Product Owner asked not to add herself to Firestore by hand. Writing her email into the rules would publish a personal email in the repo.
decisions.decision: The Firestore rules hold a SHA-256 hash of the super admin's lower-case Google email. When that account signs in for the first time, the portal creates config/access with it; the rules allow that create only for a matching hash and refuse any later change from a browser.
decisions.consequences: No manual Firestore step. Adding or changing a super admin later means a rules change (new hash) or an edit in the Firebase console. A hash of an email can be guessed by trying likely emails, so it hides the address from casual readers only.

decisions.title: With sign-in, roles come from the team; the role picker lives on only in the demo
decisions.context: The onboarding screen "What's your role?" lets anyone pick a role. With Google sign-in the admin sets roles, so picking one would contradict the team; but the live site would then lose its demo.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose: with sign-in on, roles come only from the team and the role screen is not shown; a signed-in person can open a demo (sample projects in the browser only), where they pick a role as today — offered on the no-access screen and in the sidebar account menu.
decisions.consequences: No new screen for the role picker (the existing onboarding screen is reused inside the demo). The demo must never read or write Firebase, GitHub or real projects (TC-076).

decisions.title: Project design files live on a new Project settings page
decisions.context: The first design put the project's Figma and Miro links on the Feature board; the Product Owner found that page unsuitable for them.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner chose in chat on 2026-11-27: a "Project settings" link with a gear icon is added to the sidebar's project group, for every role. Its page holds the "Design files" card; only the project admin edits it, others see the links with Open ↗. Follow-up decisions in chat, after Team access (F-015) and REQ-075 reached main: (1) the admin is the project's Admin or the super admin when sign-in is on, and the PO role from the role picker when sign-in is off (demo, local use); (2) Project settings is the last link: after Release, and after Team access's Admin-only Team link, which stays a separate item.
decisions.consequences: REQ-070, REQ-075 and their tests list Project settings as the last project link. The Admin check is a portal check only: compass/spec.json → designTool lives in the repository, so anyone with GitHub write access can still change it there (Firestore rules never see GitHub commits).

decisions.title: "Try the demo" leaves the sidebar; account actions move into an account menu
decisions.context: The sidebar footer had four loose rows (account card, "Try the demo" and "Sign out" buttons, a "My roles" line and a lone theme button). The Product Owner asked to redesign it and reviewed a mockup in chat.
decisions.decision: The Product Owner approved the mockup on 2026-11-28 with one change: "Remove try the demo in this section, the rest is fine to proceed". The footer is one account card (initial, name, role chips) that opens a menu with the email, Connections, the theme switch, Leave demo (in the demo) and Sign out.
decisions.consequences: REQ-073: AC1 changes — clicking the account card opens the account menu, and "Connections" is an item in it; AC2 changes — the theme is a "Dark theme" switch in the menu and the role picker shows only with sign-in off or in the demo. REQ-039 AC2: the read-only roles show as chips on the account card instead of a "My roles: …" line (still read-only). REQ-032 AC2: the card shows the part of the email before "@"; the full email is in the card's tooltip and at the top of the account menu. REQ-040 AC2: signed-in people on a team no longer start the demo from the sidebar; "Try the demo" stays on the "You have no access yet" screen. TC-404 checks the theme switch and the Connections item in the menu.
